close_reason: Question moot — spec author resolved the .4.11 label/body conflict by reversing the underlying design (no ownerId field, ownership is implementation-defined). See JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11 closure trail and JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12 for the revert.
description:
The /do-beads loop hit JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11 with conflicting signals and stopped per the strict label rule.

Conflict:

  - Label: 'human' — the do-beads loop rule (AGENTS.md, do-beads.md) is verbatim: 'A human label marks a durable question for the human — those beads are not actionable autonomously and must be skipped'. The label is authoritative; the loop does not read the body.

  - Body, last comment block (2026-05-11, Mark): 'Explicit authorization (2026-05-11, Mark): land the chat-types implementation ahead of the spec edit.' Per the bead body's pre-publish allowance, the implementation work is explicitly approved to land.

Downstream impact:

  - .4.11 blocks .4.3 (apply_space_patch MemoryBackend Role+Member impl, re-scoped with full permission/hierarchy/owner enforcement). Open, unlabeled, but bd correctly sees the .4.11 blocker.
  - .4.3 blocks .4.6 (integration tests for 12 Space/set sub-ops). Open, unlabeled.

So the entire Space/set chain is paused on the .4.11 label.

Question for Mark — pick one:

  (a) Drop the 'human' label from .4.11 (your explicit authorization in the body is the green light; the spec-edit task is tracked separately). The /do-beads loop will then claim .4.11, then .4.3, then .4.6 across one or more sessions. RECOMMENDED — this matches what the body says.

  (b) Keep the 'human' label on .4.11 and file a NEW unlabeled bead 'JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11-impl' for the chat-types implementation work alone, with .4.11 retained as the spec-coordination tracker. More bookkeeping but preserves the 'human label = do not touch' invariant unambiguously.

  (c) Change the loop rule to 'skip human-labeled beads UNLESS the body contains an explicit authorization marker'. NOT RECOMMENDED — that turns the label into advisory and removes the bright line that prevents the loop from spinning on questions.

Verdict for this /do-beads session: ready frontier exhausted, all remaining autonomous work is downstream of human-labeled .4.11 or sc1b (a review epic, also human-labeled).
title: Clarify: JMAP-g7wu.2.4.11 carries explicit autonomous-impl authorization in body but retains 'human' label, blocking 4.3/4.6 chain
